V.

A Reminder about Preservation of Angle Measures and Distances and an Important New Use of Preservation Properties

At the beginning of this course we made the assumptions that reflections in a line preserved distances and angle measures. This means that the reflection image of a segment has the same length as the pre-image. It also means that the reflection image of an angle has the same measure as its pre-image. You may recall the discovery that every translation can be created from a composite of reflections in parallel lines and every rotation can be created from a composite of reflections in intersecting lines. This implies that translations and rotations as well as reflections preserve distance and angle measures.

Drawing recovered as vectorsReview candidate — compare the content and labels with the original. Reference page 3.Source previewEditable representationSVG · Drawing JSON · Original file · Source PDF

Triangle ABC is in a very convenient position. One of its sides lies on the and one of its vertices is at the origin. This makes it relatively easy to determine the coordinates for points B and C in terms of the lengths of sides AB and AC and the measure of angle BAC. Once these coordinates are known, it is possible to represent first the square of the length of side BC and then that length itself.

You have seen that the length of side BC is dependent entirely upon the lengths of sides AB and BC and the measure of angle BAC. Triangle A'B'C' is in a different position, but it should not be hard to imagine that it could be the image of triangle ABC under some composite of transformations that preserve distances and angle measures. Therefore, the length of side B'C' should be the same as the length of side BC and it should have the same relationship to the lengths of sides A'B' and A'C' and the measure of angle B'A'C' as the length of side BC has to the lengths of sides AB and AC and the measure of angle BAC. This means that any relationships found to be true for some of the measures of triangles in “convenient” positions will also be true for the measures of their images under composites of reflections, translations or rotations.

Drawing recovered as vectorsReview candidate — compare the content and labels with the original. Reference page 6.Source previewEditable representationSVG · Drawing JSON · Original file · Source PDF

If [A] is used to represent the original disposition matrix and [B] is used to represent the transition matrix then the above can be summarized as follows:

To get the distribution after the first half-hour, compute the matrix product [A]*[B].

To get the distribution after the second half-hour, compute the matrix product ([A]*[B])*[B].

Because matrix multiplication is associative, the product ([A]*[B])*[B] is equivalent to [A]*([B]*[B]), which for convenience can represented as [A]*[B]2.
